# RooRooRoo

> A full-stack website monitoring application built with Next.js 16 (static
> export) and Supabase. Monitors websites for content changes and sends
> email/SMS notifications. A single Supabase Edge Function (Deno 2, composed
> from `@supabase/middleware` and `@supabase/server` — no HTTP framework)
> performs server-side checks; all frontend database access goes directly to
> Postgres via the Supabase JS client under Row Level Security. Scheduled via
> `pg_cron` + `pg_net`.

This project demonstrates a minimal Supabase server surface area architecture:
the frontend handles all database operations directly via the Supabase client
with RLS, while the Edge Function is reserved exclusively for server-only tasks
(executing monitor checks and sending notifications).

**Tech Stack**: Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, TypeScript 6, Supabase
(Postgres + Auth + Edge Functions), Deno 2, Resend (email), Twilio (SMS),
OpenAPI 3.1

**Key Constraint**: Sign-up is restricted to `@supabase.io` addresses. This is
enforced in the signup form only, not in the database — see Limitations.

## Core Documentation

[CLAUDE.md](/CLAUDE.md): Architecture overview, common commands, development
patterns, and deployment notes

## Frontend

[Frontend Package Config](/frontend/package.json): Dependencies and pnpm scripts
for the Next.js application

[Next.js Config](/frontend/next.config.mjs): Static export configuration
(`output: "export"`, trailing slashes, `agentRules: false`)

[Supabase Client](/frontend/lib/supabase/client.ts): Browser-side Supabase
client singleton using `@supabase/ssr`, typed against the generated schema

[API Client](/frontend/lib/api-client.ts): Typed fetch wrapper for the Edge
Function. The base URL is derived from `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` so auth and
the function always come from the same project

[Row Types](/frontend/lib/db.ts): Application row types derived from the
generated database types

[Monitor Scheduling](/frontend/lib/monitor-schedule.ts): pg_cron job naming and
interval-to-cron-expression conversion

[Dashboard Page](/frontend/app/dashboard/page.tsx): Main monitor list view

[New Monitor Page](/frontend/app/dashboard/new/page.tsx): Monitor creation form

[Notifications Page](/frontend/app/dashboard/notifications/page.tsx):
Notification history view

[Signup Page](/frontend/app/auth/signup/page.tsx): Email allowlist enforcement
(`NEXT_PUBLIC_ALLOWED_SIGNUP_DOMAIN` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_ALLOWED_SIGNUP_EMAILS`)

[Status Badge](/frontend/components/status-tag.tsx): Polls
`GET /functions/v1/api/openapi.json` and renders `info.version` and
`info.x-environment`

## Backend (Edge Function)

There is one Edge Function, named `api`. It has no router: `pipeline` composes
three middleware layers around a single handler, and `withOpenAPI` performs the
only path matching there is.

[API Entry Point](/supabase/functions/api/index.ts): The pipeline
(`withCORS` → `withOpenAPI` → `withSupabase` → handler) and the
`POST /check-endpoint` handler, which resolves and authorizes the monitor,
performs the check, logs it, and dispatches notifications

[CORS Middleware](/supabase/functions/_shared/with-cors.ts): Outermost layer.
Answers preflights and backfills the canonical `@supabase/supabase-js/cors`
headers onto responses from layers that short-circuit above the auth gate

[OpenAPI Middleware](/supabase/functions/_shared/with-openapi.ts): Serves the
document and rejects any path the document does not declare. `document.paths`
is the route table

[OpenAPI Document](/supabase/functions/_shared/openapi-document.ts): The API
description, and therefore the route table. Also resolves `info.version` from
`CURRENT_SHA` and `info.x-environment` from `APP_ENVIRONMENT`

[Monitor Logic](/supabase/functions/_shared/monitor.ts): Capped fetch, pattern
matching, catastrophic-backtracking screen, and check logging

[Notification Service](/supabase/functions/_shared/notifications.ts): Email
(Resend) and SMS (Twilio) dispatch, with per-channel results and notification
logging

[SMS Transport](/supabase/functions/_shared/sms-service.ts): Twilio transport
with retry

[Function Config](/supabase/functions/_shared/config.ts): Required environment
(the three `TWILIO_*` values, read at module load), notification link origin,
and the logger

[Import Map](/supabase/functions/deno.json): Pinned dependency versions for the
Deno workspace member

## Database

The schema is declarative. `supabase/schemas/` is the source of truth; edit
those files, never Studio, the SQL editor, or a hand-written migration.
`supabase/migrations/` is generated output by pg-delta and remains the deploy
artifact.

[Declarative Schema](/supabase/schemas/): Source of truth, organized as
`<schema>/<object-type>/<name>.sql`

[Monitors Table](/supabase/schemas/public/tables/monitors.sql): Monitor
definitions with RLS policies scoped to `auth.uid()`

[Monitor Logs Table](/supabase/schemas/public/tables/monitor_logs.sql): Per-check
history, readable by the owning user via a join to `monitors`

[Notifications Table](/supabase/schemas/public/tables/notifications.sql): Sent
notification records

[Profiles Table](/supabase/schemas/public/tables/profiles.sql): User profiles,
populated by the `on_auth_user_created` trigger

[Cron Headers](/supabase/schemas/public/functions/_get_cron_headers.sql): Reads
the `sb_secret_...` key from Vault (`supabase/secret_key`) and sends it as
`apikey`, deliberately with no `Authorization` bearer

[Cron Job Creation](/supabase/schemas/public/functions/create_monitor_cron_job.sql):
Schedules a `pg_net` HTTP POST per monitor, resolving URL and headers at run
time

[Check URL](/supabase/schemas/public/functions/_get_monitor_check_url.sql):
Builds the `/functions/v1/api/check-endpoint` URL from
`app.settings.api_base_url`

[Generated Types](/supabase/db/database.types.ts): TypeScript types generated
from the schema (`deno task db:gen-types`)

[Seed Data](/supabase/seed.sql): Applied on `db reset` and when a preview branch
is created

[Supabase Config](/supabase/config.toml): Local development configuration,
`[experimental.pgdelta]`, and `verify_jwt = false` for `[functions.api]`

## CI/CD

[Function Deploy Workflow](/.github/workflows/fns-push.yml): Runs
`deno task fns:checks`, sets `CURRENT_SHA`, and deploys the Edge Function on
push to `main`

[Preview Environment Workflow](/.github/workflows/preview-env.yml): Seeds Edge
Function secrets onto the PR's Supabase preview branch and posts a sticky
comment with the branch API URL and anon key

## Development Tasks

[Root Tasks](/deno.json): Deno task definitions for development, checks,
building, and database operations

[Setup Wizards](/scripts/): Interactive wizards for Twilio credentials
(`setup-twilio`), Supabase branching (`setup-branching`), and Vercel environment
sync (`setup-vercel`)

## Optional

### Endpoints

The function is served under `/functions/v1/api`. Two routes exist:

- `POST /check-endpoint` — runs one monitor check. Accepts either a user JWT
  (verified against the project JWKS) or a Supabase secret key
  (`apikey: sb_secret_...`), which is what `pg_cron` presents. In user mode the
  verified JWT subject replaces any `user_id` in the body, and `force` is
  honoured only in user mode.
- `GET /openapi.json` — public. The OpenAPI 3.1 document, whose `paths` are the
  enforced route table. Serving it also proves the function is running.

There is no `/status` route; `/openapi.json` replaced it.

### Pattern Matching

The monitor check system supports three pattern types:

- `contains`: Case-insensitive substring match with context snippets
- `not_contains`: Inverse match (content must NOT contain pattern)
- `regex`: Regular expression match (case-insensitive)

Pattern matching implementation: `checkPattern` at
`/supabase/functions/_shared/monitor.ts:359`.

A `regex` pattern is screened by `findUnsafeRegexConstruct`
(`/supabase/functions/_shared/monitor.ts:203`) and rejected if it can backtrack
catastrophically — a quantifier applied to a group that can match the same input
more than one way, such as `(a+)+$`. A match is synchronous and uninterruptible
on the edge worker, so no timer can stop a runaway one. The screen is a
heuristic, not a proof; a linear-time engine (RE2 via WASM) is the complete fix
and is deliberately deferred.

### Monitor Check Flow

1. User creates monitor via frontend → direct Supabase insert
2. Frontend calls the `create_monitor_cron_job()` database function
3. `pg_cron` schedules a `pg_net` HTTP POST of `{ monitor_id, user_id }` to
   `/functions/v1/api/check-endpoint`
4. The Edge Function fetches the URL, evaluates the pattern, writes a
   `monitor_logs` row, and updates `monitors.last_status` / `last_checked`
5. Notifications are sent on the first check, on a status change, or when a
   signed-in user passes `force` — see `getNotificationSpec` at
   `/supabase/functions/_shared/monitor.ts:471`
6. The frontend re-queries `monitors`, `monitor_logs` and `notifications`
   directly under RLS. There are no Realtime subscriptions yet.

### Authentication Architecture

- **Frontend**: Supabase Auth (email/password); authenticated users access their
  own data via RLS
- **Edge Function**: `withSupabase` with `auth: ['user', 'secret']`. `user`
  verifies the JWT against the project JWKS; `secret` matches an `sb_secret_`
  key in the `apikey` header. `/openapi.json` never reaches this layer, because
  `withOpenAPI` answers it first
- **Client privilege**: a user gets the RLS-scoped `ctx.supabase`; cron gets
  `ctx.supabaseAdmin`, having no `auth.uid()` to scope by. The handler filters
  by `user_id` regardless, so RLS is a backstop rather than the only control
- **Platform gate**: `verify_jwt = false` for `[functions.api]`, because the
  platform's blanket check is equivalent to `auth: 'user'` on every route and
  would reject both the public document and the cron call. The gate moves into
  the function, it is not removed
- **CORS**: the canonical wildcard set from `@supabase/supabase-js/cors`. The
  API is protected by credentials, not by origin
- **Database**: all tables have RLS policies scoping access to `auth.uid()`
- **Secrets**: the cron secret key lives in Supabase Vault
  (`supabase/secret_key`), with `app.settings.secret_key` as a fallback

### Limitations

- Sign-up is restricted to `@supabase.io` addresses by the signup form only, and
  is configurable via `NEXT_PUBLIC_ALLOWED_SIGNUP_DOMAIN` /
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_ALLOWED_SIGNUP_EMAILS`. Nothing in Postgres or Supabase Auth
  enforces it
- Content must exist in raw HTML (no JavaScript-rendered content detection)
- Monitor checks time out after 30 seconds, covering the body read as well as
  the connection; bodies are buffered up to 5MB and regex matches against at
  most the first 512KB
- Does not respect `robots.txt` directives
- `pg_cron` has a one-minute floor, and intervals that do not divide evenly into
  an hour fall back to every five minutes
